question: Does the Quezon advisory label “Silongin Lagda” identify the EMB-listed Silongin River in San Francisco, Quezon?
purpose: Record the official river name and municipality while preventing an unsupported merge of the advisory’s compound label with a named river.

findings.evidence: Quezon Provincial Government General Flood Advisory No. 14, issued 7 August 2026, includes the exact compound label “Silongin Lagda” in its list of Quezon rivers and tributaries likely to be affected.
doesNotSupport: whether “Silongin Lagda” is one feature or two

findings.evidence: DENR-EMB’s National State of the Brown Environment Report 2016–2021, Table 3.3, lists “SILONGIN RIVER” under “SAN FRANCISCO, QUEZON,” type River, source-reported classification B/C, year classified 2019.
doesNotSupport: a match to the full advisory label “Silongin Lagda”

findings.evidence: The Quezon provincial municipality directory lists Silongin among the barangays of San Francisco, Quezon.
supports: official administrative locality context for the name Silongin
doesNotSupport: a link between the barangay and the EMB waterbody beyond the shared locality/name context

crosswalk.resolutionLevel: partial name/locality association only; advisory label not linked to river lead
crosswalk.confidence: EMB independently names Silongin River in San Francisco, Quezon, and the provincial directory lists a San Francisco barangay named Silongin. The Quezon advisory uses the compound text “Silongin Lagda.” No reviewed official source explains “Lagda” or establishes whether it is a second feature, alternate name, or part of the same river label.
crosswalk.mergeDecision: Add Silongin River as an independent official source-named research lead. Keep “Silongin Lagda” unresolved in the advisory queue; do not add it as an alias or attribute the advisory to Silongin River until an official source explains the compound label.

reuseAndLimitations: The EMB report permits educational or non-profit reproduction with acknowledgement, but that is not an open-data license or public-app/derived-database approval. Only minimal factual metadata is retained.
The source-reported B/C classification and 2019 classification year are historical table metadata, not current water-quality measurements or ecological suitability.
The province directory supports a barangay/locality name, not the river route or a feature boundary.
The Quezon advisory is a dated historical notice, not current hazard guidance.
No fish checklist, occurrence, current presence/absence, salinity, access, fishing rule, safety advice, or geometry is established.
nextActions: Seek an official LGU, EMB, or hydrography source that explains the “Lagda” portion of the advisory label before linking it to the Silongin River lead.
Review site-resolved fish evidence and route-scale hydrography for Silongin River as separate research tasks.
